To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
atherectomy is more effective than balloon angioplasties for ostial lesions, bifurcations, complex lesions and lesions with dissections or thrombi.

the use of atherectomy is associated with a reduction in the need for urgent coronary artery bypass grafting, and that the use of the atherectomy device is associated with a higher rate of major adverse cardiac events than the use of balloon angioplasties.
directional coronary atherotomy is a safe and effective method of treating certain types of coronary lesions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the effects of the coronary atherectomy on the coronary artery.
the development of new methods for the diagnosis and treatment of coronary artery disease.

the following: 1) the role of atherectomy in the treatment of specific coronary lesions; 2) the effect of atherectomy on acute complications and late restenosis; and 3) the role of adjunctive devices in the treatment of coronary lesions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
directional coronary atherectectomy is a useful adjunct to balloon angioplasty and is most effective in specific types of lesions.
directional atherectectomy appears to be most useful in proximally located, noncalcified coronary lesions that are large (> 2 mm) and discrete.

directional atherectomies are most likely to be beneficial in proximal to middle coronary segments, in ostial lesions and bifurcation stentoses, in proximal left anterior descendent stenoses, in discrete saphenious graft lesions, in complex or thrombus containing lesions, in highly eccentric lesions, in patients with limited angiographic success after balloon angioplasty due to elastic recoil, and in patients with recurrent thrombosis or dissection after angioplasty.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the indications and contraindications for directional atherectomy remain to be defined.
atherectomy is not the answer to all of the limitations of balloon PTCA.
directional coronary atherectomies should be reserved for patients with complex coronary lesions who have failed or are likely to fail balloon angioplasty.
The main takeaway from our work is that
directional atheroectomy is a safe and effective treatment for coronary artery disease.
directional atherectomies are useful in ostial lesions, bifurcations, proximal LAD lesions, and saphenous graft lesions.

directional coronary atherectomies are useful in the following situations: ostial lesions, bifurcations, proximal LAD lesions, discrete sapphenous vein graft stentosis, complex lesions, and highly eccentric lesions.
